correctness.rationale:
A term-overlap graph of maximum degree one decomposes into physically disjoint Pauli components, so the thermal state factorizes. For a two-term pair with zero local anticommutations choose local product joint eigenbases; with exactly one, condition on commuting sites and diagonalize the remaining single qubit. With even d>=2 the Pauli strings commute, and rho=2^-k(I+sP+tQ+stPQ), after coefficient-sign normalization. The coefficient-l1 Pauli mixture proves sufficiency s+t+st<=1, while a one-site partial transpose has eigenvalue 2^-k(1-s-t-st) on a common (-,-) eigenspace, proving necessity. With odd d>=3 the global strings anticommute; exact exponentiation gives rho=2^-k(I+uP+vQ), and the same l1 lemma suffices, whereas a two-locally-incompatible-site Bloch-ball/Cauchy–Schwarz witness bounds |

|+||<=1 for every fully separable state, proving necessity. The three-qubit XXX/ZZZ Gibbs example violates this witness above atan h(1/sqrt2)/sqrt2 yet all its partial transposes equal rho. Independent small matrix PT eigenvalues and witness checks confirm signs, with the unrestricted argument wholly algebraic.
residual_risks: The result addresses full separability, not all cut-by-cut bipartite separabilities; PPT example is not proof of PPT-bound entanglement under each bipartition.
Proof uses each pair’s specified nonzero Pauli terms and actual local incompatibility count; not applicable to three-or-more-term overlap components.
